title: The Absolute Equality Mural
bio: Houston-based artist Reginald C. Adams is known for creating powerful public art that celebrates history, healing, and community. In Galveston, he led the creation of the Absolute Equality mural, a landmark tribute to Juneteenth and the ongoing journey toward freedom and equality.
desc: The Absolute Equality mural in Galveston honors the birthplace of Juneteenth and celebrates the ongoing pursuit of freedom, justice, and equality.

title: Greetings from Galveston
bio: Gabriel Prusmack is a Galveston-based artist known for his bright colors, bold designs, and joyful public art. His work often blends playful imagery, identity, and island spirit, helping bring color and creativity to public spaces throughout Galveston.
desc: Greetings From Galveston mural is one of the island’s most recognizable photo spots. Painted in the style of a vintage postcard, the mural welcomes visitors with colorful letters that celebrate Galveston’s beaches, landmarks, history, and coastal character.

title: Postoffice Street Mural Collection
desc: The Postoffice Mural Collection began as Galveston’s Kindness Mural, a colorful reminder to lead with compassion and community spirit. Over time, it has evolved into a quarterly rotating mural project where local and visiting artists showcase their creativity during ArtWalk. Now led by local artist Justin Lopez, the collection continues to bring fresh energy, new voices, and ever-changing public art to Postoffice Street.

title: I Love Galveston Mural
bio: Gabriel Prusmack is a Texas muralist based in Galveston whose work is known for its vibrant color, playful imagination, and large-scale public art. His murals bring energy to everyday spaces and help turn city walls into joyful landmarks.
desc: The I Love Galveston mural at 24th and The Strand is a colorful celebration of island life. Filled with playful sea creatures and a bold red heart, it has become a fun photo stop that captures Galveston’s coastal charm and community pride.

title: Stay Beach Box Mural
bio: Carlos Villasana, also known as Loz Paints, is a Galveston-based muralist and art educator. His work brings bold color, public art, and creative energy to local spaces, transforming walls and surfaces into eye-catching pieces that reflect the spirit of the island.
desc: Stay Beach Box Mural brings a bright coastal splash to 25th and Market Street. Painted in spray paint, the mural adds color and island personality to the side of Stay Beach Box and helps welcome visitors into Galveston’s growing public art scene.

title: Mermaids
desc: Mermaid Mural at MarMo Plaza brings a dreamy, coastal energy to Market Street. Featuring mystical mermaid imagery, the mural reflects Galveston’s connection to the Gulf, imagination, and creative self-expression
